articles.originalTitle: Tammy Nguyen’s New Opera Will Be the Coda to the Venice Biennale - Hyperallergic
articles.title: Tammy Nguyen Opera to Be Presented at the 61st Venice Biennale Closing Program
articles.excerpt: Artist Tammy Nguyen will present the foreword to her debut opera blending the impacts of the Vietnam War and Plato's philosophy at the Venice Biennale closing.
articles.content: Artist Tammy Nguyen will present the foreword to her debut opera Timaeus and The Teacher at the 61st Venice Biennale closing program on November 13 and 14. The aria serves as an entry point to the unfinished opera, which traces the national and ideological impacts of the Vietnam War and fuses Plato’s theories of the cosmos with questions of identity. Inspired by her father's experiences as a refugee in the South China Sea, Nguyen centers the performance around a Vietnamese English teacher attempting to flee Saigon by boat two years after North Vietnamese forces captured the capital in 1975. Grammy-nominated tenor Brian Vu will sing the libretto, accompanied by dancers maneuvering around a tapestry composed of flags. Commissioned and produced by Wesleyan University, where Nguyen teaches, the opera echoes themes from her paintings on view at the biennale's Central Pavilion through November 22. The tapestry extends upon her 2024 exhibition at the Sarasota Art Museum. Choreographed by Jamal Jackson, the performance configurations include mountain ranges, a ship, and cosmological diagrams. Composer Neely Bruce remixed national anthems into the musical score, while Nguyen assembled the libretto by breaking down traditional English language structures through a fractal sequence. While the full production timeline remains unclear, the artist aims for completion by fall 2029.

articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Opens Exhibition Exploring Pictorialism and Art Photography
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is hosting a new exhibition focusing on pictorialism, the first international art photography movement, featuring over 200 rare vintage photographic prints.
articles.content: Tate Modern presents Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, an exhibition running from 14 October 2026 to 21 February 2027. The display features over 200 rare vintage photographic prints and explores pictorialism, recognized as the first international art photography movement. Emerging in the 1880s, pictorialist photographers sought to establish photography as a genuine art form comparable to painting through imaginative darkroom experiments and studio techniques. The exhibition highlights complex developing and printing processes, negative manipulation, and various paper types used by these artists. Visitors can explore a working darkroom within the exhibition space to learn vintage printing techniques. Highlights include works by Alvin Langdon Coburn, Cavendish Morton's character portraits, platinum and bromoil print techniques, Soichi Sunami's dance collaborations, and modernist works by members of Brazil's Foto Cine Clube Bandeirante.

articles.originalTitle: House museum of Spanish ‘master of light’ Joaquín Sorolla reopens in Madrid - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Joaquin Sorolla Museum in Madrid Reopens Following First Phase of Expansion
articles.excerpt: Spanish painter Joaquín Sorolla's home and museum in Madrid reopens with a new extension following a two-year restoration and expansion project.
articles.content: The Sorolla Museum in Madrid, operating in the historic home and atelier of Spanish painter Joaquín Sorolla y Bastida, reopens to visitors on October 15 after a two-year closure. While the historic residence remains closed for restoration, the first phase of the €14 million project is now complete, adding a 1,698 sq. m extension featuring new exhibition spaces, an auditorium, and storage facilities. Museum director Enrique Valera noted that the previous facilities had become inadequate for visitor services and collection management. Built on adjacent properties acquired by the Ministry of Culture in 2009, the new extension was designed by the architecture firm Nieto Sobejano. The new facilities provide improved conditions for storing the museum's collection and conducting restoration work, alongside step-free access throughout the site. Restoration work on the historic residence, covering both its interior and exterior, is expected to take approximately two years.

articles.originalTitle: Anne Carson Wins the Nobel Prize, and Everyone Is Happy - ArtReview
articles.title: Canadian Writer and Translator Anne Carson Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.excerpt: Canadian writer, translator, and poet Anne Carson has been awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature, announced by the Swedish Academy on October 8.
articles.content: Canadian writer, translator, essayist, and poet Anne Carson has been awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature. Swedish Academy secretary Ingrid Carlberg announced the prize on October 8, noting during the announcement that Carson stated she was currently in Iceland listening to the wind. Since her 1986 work Eros the Bittersweet, Carson has published over 20 books spanning poetry, essays, and translations. Beginning as a translator and classics teacher, Carson gained widespread recognition for works such as If Not, Winter, her translations of the ancient Greek poet Sappho. Her writings consistently explore female figures, high femininity, and intertextual depth while experimenting with literary forms, a shifting structure she attributes to boredom. Carson has incorporated diverse philosophical and historical references, ranging from Hegel to Ovid, across her poetry and prose. She has also experimented with the physical format of books in projects like Nox and Float. Influential to contemporary artists and writers, Carson's oeuvre bridges visual art and poetry through scholarly intensity combined with irony and precise linguistic craftsmanship.

articles.originalTitle: Chen Qiulin: Where Does the Past Live? - ArtReview
articles.title: Chen Qiulin: Heartland Exhibition at Shenzhen Museum Explores Human Displacement
articles.excerpt: Spanning over two decades, Chen Qiulin's exhibition at Pingshan Art Museum examines human displacement through video and photographic works rooted in her hometown's submersion by the Three Gorges Dam.
articles.content: Growing up in Wanzhou, Chongqing, artist Chen Qiulin witnessed her hometown fall directly in the path of the Three Gorges Dam, which submerged nearly half of it upon completion. This profound transformation prompted the artist to interrogate human displacement. Showcasing a selection of works spanning over two decades, the exhibition at Pingshan Art Museum highlights how memory and home intersect with large-scale societal shifts. In the 2002 single-channel video Farewell Poem, filmed at a demolition site prior to the town's submersion, Chen acts out passages from classic Chinese opera. The Three Gorges Dam project precipitated the migration of more than 260,000 residents within Chongqing. Addressing this uprooted population in the 2007 video work The Garden, Chen employed local porters to wander through the urban landscape carrying oversized artificial peony bouquets. Furthermore, in the Another Day series, she examines rural Guizhou communities where elderly women remain in ancestral villages while younger family members migrate to larger cities. Set within a newly developing district of Shenzhen defined by transient communities, the museum setting mirrors the very shifts the artist interrogates.

articles.originalTitle: Long-Awaited Le Large Finally Opens on Paris’s Idyllic Île Seguin - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Paris's New Contemporary Art Center Le Large Opens on Île Seguin
articles.excerpt: Le Large, a new contemporary art center on Île Seguin in western Paris, occupies a former industrial site. Designed by RCR Arquitectes, the venue opens with the exhibition Moteur Imaginaire.
articles.content: France's newest contemporary art center, Le Large, has opened on Île Seguin in Boulogne-Billancourt in the western suburbs of Paris. Once home to a Renault factory, the island is being transformed as part of a 450 million euro cultural development known as Pointe des Arts. Designed by Pritzker Prize-winning RCR Arquitectes, the building features a copper-colored anodized-aluminum facade with diamond-shaped elements. Operating with an estimated annual budget of 5 million euros, the center features flexible exhibition spaces capable of hosting either single large-scale shows or multiple simultaneous exhibitions. Around 40 percent of its public-facing spaces are free to enter. The institution operates on a hybrid model combining a nonprofit association and a commercial entity for private events. The inaugural exhibition, Moteur Imaginaire, is curated by Cecilia Alemani and brings together more than 100 works by 55 artists from 23 countries. Drawing on the island's industrial history, the display incorporates 50 pieces from the Renault collection alongside historical photographs, following a spatial layout that evokes automotive assembly lines.

articles.originalTitle: Carmody Groarke’s Addition to Design Museum Gent Reads as a Manifesto on Sustainable Design - Architectural Record
articles.title: Carmody Groarke Unveils Sustainable Extension for Design Museum Gent
articles.excerpt: London practice Carmody Groarke, alongside local firms, has completed a sustainable five-story museum extension in Gent utilizing locally sourced waste materials.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent has opened a new 23,680-square-foot extension designed by London-based Carmody Groarke in collaboration with local practices ATAMA and RE-ST. Inserted into a vacant plot within the historic center of Ghent, the five-story wing establishes continuous circulation routes through the museum's existing historic buildings. To address ecological challenges, the architects partnered with Belgian consultant BC Materials to develop the Gent Waste Brick. Comprising crushed concrete, glass, and porcelain sourced within a five-mile radius, the 82,000 unfired masonry units were cured in hydraulic lime to significantly reduce embodied carbon. The structural system relies on solid cross-laminated timber walls and laminated veneer lumber beams rather than traditional concrete frameworks. Additional sustainable features include entrance gates 3D-printed from recycled aluminum by studio Unfold, and lobby floors lined with end-grain wood blocks salvaged from a former tobacco factory. The uppermost floor houses a public event space beneath an expressive timber roof offering views of the surrounding urban context.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026: performances, lectures, discussions, roundtables - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Art Exhibition Announces Public Programme for Final Days
articles.excerpt: The final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition in Venice will feature a public programme of performances, lectures, roundtables, and an assembly of artist-led collectives at the Arsenale.
articles.content: During the final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition in Venice, the spaces of the Arsenale will host a public programme comprising performances, lectures, debates, and roundtables. Curated by Koyo Kouoh under the title In Minor Keys, the events will run from November 13 to November 22. The schedule features special performances by artists including Laurie Anderson, Ziad Antar, rana elnemr, and Tammy Nguyen. Additionally, an Assembly will bring together ten artist-led organizations and collectives from capital cities, provincial centers, and rural communities to share creative practices and reflect on pedagogy, research, and community care. Panel sessions will examine seed projects and the establishment of spaces that offer practitioners time to convene and collaborate, while lectures by speakers such as Felwine Sarr will address relationality, hospitality, and global mobility. The program will also host roundtables reflecting on the legacies of deceased artists featured in the exhibition, including Issa Samb, Beverly Buchanan, Nancy Brooks Brody, Seyni Awa Camara, and Pauline Oliveros.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Explores the Art and Fashion Culture of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain is hosting The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, bringing together art, fashion, photography, and design drawing on curator Edward Enninful's experience.
articles.content: Tate Britain is presenting The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, examining a period defined by bold creativity and a rebellious spirit. Drawing on curator Edward Enninful's experience, the exhibition brings together photography, fashion, art, and design to explore a moment when a new generation transformed culture. The exhibition features works by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Visitors can experience the energy and cultural shifts of a decade that broke down boundaries between art, fashion, and popular culture. Key pieces in the selection include Mark Leckey's video work tracing British dance music culture, Yinka Shonibare's reimagining of colonial histories, and Steve McQueen's silent film Bear. The exhibition is on view from 8 October 2026 to 14 February 2027.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: Holst Architecture Completes Mass-Timber East County Library in Oregon
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture and Adjaye Associates, the 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham opens as a 163 million dollar mass-timber civic landmark.
articles.content: Located in Gresham, Oregon, the East County Library spans 95,000 square feet and represents a 163 million dollar civic investment designed by Holst Architecture in collaboration with Adjaye Associates. Built on a former transit park-and-ride parcel, the two-story structure stands 59 feet tall and features a board-formed concrete base supporting exposed heavy-timber columns. The design process involved extensive community outreach, leading to programmatic inclusions such as dedicated meeting spaces, recording studios, and an auditorium for local organizations. Working alongside mass-timber specialists Timberlab, the design team utilized 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed without additional fire-resistant treatments. The interior accommodates open book stacks for 200,000 volumes, centered around a double-height atrium with a spiral staircase. Mechanical equipment and ductwork were strategically integrated into the basement and floor reveals to preserve the visual warmth of the timber structure. Overseen by Multnomah County Library representatives, the facility addresses demographic shifts and long-unmet regional needs in East Multnomah County by providing an open public platform for the surrounding communities.

articles.originalTitle: Boucheron Amps Up Its Spotlight in the U.S. with New Christie’s Exhibition - Robb Report
articles.title: French Jewelry House Boucheron Expands U.S. Presence with Christie's Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Boucheron is connecting with U.S. clients through a monographic exhibition at Christie's New York headquarters, showcasing its historical heritage and innovative high jewelry.
articles.content: French jewelry maison Boucheron opened a ten-day exhibition titled Boucheron: In Focus, a Monograph of a Visionary at Christie's New York headquarters. Following the opening of its North American flagship on Madison Avenue two years ago, the brand is using the exhibition to strengthen its U.S. presence. CEO Hélène Poulit-Duquesne stated the event aims to communicate the maison's nearly 170-year history of historical craftsmanship alongside its innovative spirit. The exhibition features archival pieces from founder Frédéric Boucheron's era, including Lady Harcourt's 1924 diamond tiara and Mrs. Mackay's laurel wreath necklace. Organized by themes of architecture, nature, history, and innovation, the display also incorporates recent high jewelry collections such as Impermanence and Human Nature, showcasing experimental materials and artistic techniques.

articles.originalTitle: tarek atoui turns tate modern’s turbine hall into a giant experimental orchestra - Designboom
articles.title: Tarek Atoui Transforms London's Tate Modern Into an Experimental Orchestra
articles.excerpt: Lebanese artist and composer Tarek Atoui is transforming the iconic Turbine Hall at London's Tate Modern with a sound installation. Created for the 11th Hyundai Commission, the site-specific work brings together experimental instruments and architectural acoustic experiences.
articles.content:
Lebanese artist and composer Tarek Atoui is transforming the industrial interior of Tate Modern’s Turbine Hall in London with a large-scale sound installation. Created for the 11th Hyundai Commission, the site-specific work brings together experimental musical instruments, sculptural structures, and acoustic experiences that extend beyond conventional listening. Rather than simply filling the hall with music, Atoui approaches the architecture itself as an instrument, exploring how sound travels through space, materials, and the human body.

Based in Paris, Atoui has spent over two decades challenging the boundaries between music, sculpture, and performance in collaboration with craftspeople, engineers, and fellow artists. Glass, water, ceramics, and mechanical systems frequently appear in his practice. For his latest commission, he has developed four families of instruments selected for their relationship with the hall's acoustics, including computer-controlled sheng instruments, oversized karnai horns, and Korean drums. Large fabric elements developed with Satoshi Kondo and Issey Miyake, coated with conductive graphite paint, act as oscillators producing sounds through movement.

Curated by Nabila Abdel Nabi and Dina Akhmadeeva, the exhibition will be open to the public from October 13, 2026, through April 11, 2027. Over forty musicians are expected to engage with the installation through live performances during its six-month run.

articles.originalTitle: BIG wins ‘fountain plaza tirana’ competition with building lifted above the public realm - Designboom
articles.title: Bjarke Ingels Group Wins Fountain Plaza Tirana Architectural Competition
articles.excerpt: Bjarke Ingels Group has won the international design competition for Fountain Plaza Tirana. The winning proposal raises the building above a park-like public realm using slender columns and a translucent facade to maintain openness.
articles.content:
Bjarke Ingels Group has won the international design competition for Fountain Plaza Tirana with a proposal that raises the building above a park-like public realm in Tirana, Albania. The project combines elevated building volumes, a translucent facade, and a network of slender columns to maintain an architecture open to the surrounding landscape.

The team approaches the site as a continuous public environment, integrating an open-access library, community facilities, and a covered public auditorium with greenery. A dense field of slender, cane-like columns lifts the structure above ground level, leaving space for public activity and allowing pedestrians to move through the footprint. The jury praised this permeability, describing the scheme as one of the most generous park experiences among the entries. Upper floors are set back to bring natural light into the covered auditorium and make room for planting.

The proposal considers pedestrianizing the adjacent traffic road and extending the park toward neighboring areas. The design also integrates the adjacent canal as an active component, linking the waterway to the environmental and microclimatic conditions of the site.

articles.originalTitle: OMA adapts historic houston coffee plant into music and arts academy - Designboom
articles.title: OMA Adapts Historic Houston Coffee Plant into Music and Arts Academy
articles.excerpt: Architecture practice OMA is transforming Houston's 1930s J.A. Folger & Co. coffee plant into the Frank Liu Jr. Academy for Music and Arts.
articles.content: Led by OMA partner Jason Long and project architect Salome Nikuradze, the 6,050-square-meter project is located along Houston’s Buffalo Bayou East corridor. The initiative adapts a historic 1930s industrial building into a tuition-free public charter school focused on music and creative learning. Drawing on Montessori principles, the architecture organizes learning across three stories based on student developmental stages, arranging classrooms around shared commons that OMA terms neighborhoods. To address the challenge of bringing natural light into the industrial structure, classrooms line the perimeter while circular skylights illuminate central shared spaces. The design preserves original industrial elements, including restored street-facing windows and a landscaped courtyard with colorful geometric window divisions. Additional architectural features include a double-height cafetorium and an opening in the floor connecting two libraries shaped like the letter 'f', referencing musical notation and string instruments.

articles.originalTitle: Celebrating 20 years of The Jameel Gallery at the V&A - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: The Jameel Gallery at the Victoria and Albert Museum Celebrates Twentieth Anniversary
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is marking the twentieth anniversary of the Jameel Gallery, home to its Islamic Middle East arts collection, with new displays and events.
articles.content: Opened in July 2006 at V&A South Kensington, the Jameel Gallery brings together approximately 400 objects spanning from the 8th century to the present day across Spain and Central Asia. The free-to-visit gallery displays ceramics, carpets, metalwork, woodwork, glass, and manuscripts made possible through the support of the Jameel family. Marking its 20th anniversary this year, the gallery has hosted public programs, conferences, and live craft demonstrations, including Egyptian textile artist Hany Abd El-Kader showcasing cotton applique and embroidery artist Yulduz Mukhiddinova leading suzani sessions. Middle East curator Mariam Rosser-Owen noted that the museum's collecting history of Middle Eastern art began in the 1850s to improve British design. Fady Jameel stated that the partnership remains committed to preserving artistic traditions while reaching new audiences. Key objects on display include the 1539-1540 Ardabil Carpet, an illuminated carpet from Iran, a Fatimid rock crystal ewer, a towering minbar made for Sultan Qaitbay, and a 15th-century lustreware bowl from Malaga. The gallery is located in Room 42 at V&A South Kensington and requires no booking for entry.

articles.originalTitle: How an Isle of Wight farm building became an architect’s modern-day retreat - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Historic Farm Building on the Isle of Wight Transformed Into Modern Retreat
articles.excerpt: Studio Weave founder Je Ahn has transformed a modest 158 sq m barn on the Isle of Wight into a pared-down personal retreat. Guided by deep reuse, the project preserves original materials while adapting the agricultural structure for modern habitation.
articles.content: Studio Weave practice founder Je Ahn acquired an existing 158 sq m barn within a working farm near Cowes on the UK's Isle of Wight, transforming it into a pared-down personal retreat. Operating with a limited budget and the unique advantage of being his own client, Ahn approached the redesign with an emphasis on flexibility and comfort. The Studio Weave team preserved much of the 50-plus-year-old original fabric, leaving original materials exposed and repairing them to meet 21st-century habitation standards. The heart of the home features a large open-plan kitchen and living area with expansive windows, leading through a small corridor to three bedrooms. Meticulous detailing and craftwork were completed in collaboration with Mike at Imphouse and his team, while the landscape was produced alongside Tom Massey Studio. Grounded in the concept of deep reuse, the design repurposes materials found on site for both their narrative and practical value. The minimal interventions ensure the agricultural building retains its historical integrity while functioning as a contemporary residential space.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.

articles.originalTitle: Where 60 Years of Master Craftsmanship Meets Modern Luxury Tech - WWD
articles.title: Adrian Jules Combines HandTailored Craftsmanship With Modern Enterprise Technology
articles.excerpt: Established in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier has developed an enterprise resource planning system to streamline operations in luxury custom clothing.
articles.content: Founded in Rochester, New York, in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier integrates over 60 years of hand-tailored craftsmanship with enterprise technology. The company developed an internal Enterprise Resource Planning system to track garments from initial order entry through workshop cutting, construction, and accounting. The platform serves as a central hub for private-label tailors and retailers, offering real-time visibility into fabric availability, pricing, and high-resolution visuals from global vendors. Platinum division CEO Alex Roberti emphasized the company's commitment to family-run values and high quality, while operations president Arnie Roberti noted that technology has streamlined pattern introduction and inventory tracking. Additionally, Adrian Jules has expanded its offerings by creating pattern designs specifically adapted to women's body shapes, helping retail partners capture a broader luxury market.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Moldova Pavilion: HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Moldova Pavilion to Host Roundtable on Art and Crisis
articles.excerpt: A roundtable discussion at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice will explore how war and contemporary crises reshape future imaginations.
articles.content: The Moldova Pavilion at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice will host a roundtable discussion on 16 October 2026, exploring how war and contemporary crises alter approaches to the future. Organised in collaboration with the European Cultural Foundation and the European Council on Foreign Relations, the public event runs from 16:00 to 18:00. The programme begins with a church tour led by Don Gianmatteo Caputo, priest, architect, and administrator of the church. The discussion takes its starting point from the Republic of Moldova's inaugural official participation in the International Art Exhibition, featuring drone-supported displays. Moving outward from Moldova's geopolitical realities, the conversation will examine the future of Europe and the ways cultural practice and artistic imagination respond to conflict. Speakers include former Deputy Prime Minister Nicu Popescu, André Wilkens, and Silvia Eiblmayr. The session will be moderated by Adelina Luft.

articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Green Building Market Deepens While Navigating Cost and Policy Challenges
articles.excerpt: While sustainable design and contracting revenues are on the rise, industry stakeholders are grappling with challenges such as federal incentive rollbacks, rising costs, and data gaps.
articles.content: Last year, the revenue of the top 100 green design firms increased by 17.1% to $11.8 billion, while international green design revenue rose 18.3% to $2.15 billion. The revenue of the top 100 green contractors also increased by 5.9% to $101.9 billion. While growth varied across markets, the largest increases were observed in industrial processes, hotels, and health care. However, industry experts point out that the rollback of federal sustainability incentives has created a ripple effect on project costs. Jill Kurtz from Stantec notes that many projects face uncertainties regarding real-world performance, emphasizing that decisions should be grounded in building science and operational data rather than certifications alone. Renée Azerbegi of Mead & Hunt states that shifting policy priorities and reduced incentive programs have generated funding uncertainty. Anica Landreneau from HOK reported that clients are increasingly concerned about grid reliability and energy resilience. Contractors suggest that bringing designers and trade partners together early on is critical in translating sustainability goals into practical decisions.

articles.originalTitle: Members' Tour: The Genius of Renaissance Sculptors: Donatello and Michelangelo - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Schedules Members Tour Featuring Donatello and Michelangelo
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting an exclusive members tour exploring the works of Donatello and Michelangelo with a guide. The event takes place on 26 November 2026.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum has announced an exclusive members tour designed to explore the works of Donatello and Michelangelo within its permanent collection. The event is scheduled for Thursday, 26 November 2026, from 15.00 to 16.00 at Blavatnik Hall in V&A South Kensington, London. Tickets are priced at 15.00 pounds, which includes light refreshments served in the Members Room following the tour. Guided by Boe Paschall, the tour examines how both Renaissance sculptors revolutionised and modernised the art form amidst an age of religious and political upheaval. Participants will hear revealing backstories regarding the Protestant Reformation, the extravagance of popes, and church turmoil prompted by nudity. Organisers note that the tour involves extensive walking and stairs, advising members with accessibility questions to contact the events team directly. V&A membership benefits include free entry to exhibitions, dedicated events, and retail discounts.

articles.originalTitle: More Than 200 Mary McFadden Garments On Display at Woodmere Art Museum - WWD
articles.title: More Than 200 Mary McFadden Garments On Display at Woodmere Art Museum
articles.excerpt: The Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia has launched a dedicated exhibition featuring more than 200 original garments and accessories by Mary McFadden, accessible both online and in person.
articles.content: The Woodmere Art Museum, an institution focused on the art and artists of Philadelphia, has established a dedicated space to exhibit more than 200 original garments and accessories by Mary McFadden. Received by the museum last October, the collection includes silk items, separates, embellished tunics, daywear, and dramatic couture pieces. It also features the designer's renowned gowns, celebrated for innovative pleating techniques that give fabric a sculptural quality while allowing fluid movement around the body. William Valerio, Woodmere director and chief executive officer, stated that the work offers an extraordinary lens to explore the intersection of fashion, art, craftsmanship, and cultural history. John McFadden, the designer's brother, expressed satisfaction that the collection found a home at Woodmere. A significant portion of the collection was provided by Joan Olden, who served as president of Mary McFadden Inc. for many years. Beginning this month, the museum is offering in-person member tours, with a special borrowing program expected to launch in the coming weeks.

articles.originalTitle: Cosima von Bonin’s soft toys storm the Petit Palais - Art Basel
articles.title: Cosima von Bonin Unveils Dollys & Beaux Exhibition at Petit Palais
articles.excerpt: German artist Cosima von Bonin presents the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais for Art Basel Paris's public program, bringing together her fabric sculptures and soft toy figures.
articles.content: Kenyan-born German artist Cosima von Bonin is presenting the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais as part of Art Basel Paris's public program. The exhibition features large-scale soft-stuffed leather, velvet, and mohair sculptures created by the artist. These figures, which previously appeared in Loewe's Fall/Winter 2026 collection show, establish a dialogue between contemporary art and fashion. The presented works include velvet St. Bernard dog sculptures with plush barrels around their necks, sea scallops, a hermit crab, an octopus, and a killer whale. Spanning a career of over 40 years, von Bonin's installations encourage open-ended interpretations from viewers rather than imposing a single narrative. Miu Miu serves as the official partner for the public program. Dollys & Beaux is on view at the Petit Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026, while Art Basel Paris takes place at the Grand Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: In Transit with artist Nour Jaouda - Art Basel
articles.title: Exploring Space, Memory, and Movement with Artist Nour Jaouda
articles.excerpt: In an interview as part of the In Transit series produced in partnership with Qatar Airways, Libyan artist Nour Jaouda discusses how travel, memory, and cultural mobility shape her textile and sculptural practices.
articles.content: Working with sculptural, hand-dyed textiles and hanging fiber installations, Libyan artist Nour Jaouda explores how spaces embody memory. Based between Cairo and London, Jaouda notes that moving between diverse social and cultural landscapes has informed her visual language. A 2023 visit to Benghazi, where she reconnected with a decades-old fig tree in her grandmother's garden, directly influenced her tapestries created for the 2024 Venice Biennale. Explaining that carrying a prayer mat during travels grounds her, she emphasizes the importance of this ritual. Connecting color to movement, Jaouda employs deconstruction and décollage techniques to create meaning through unmaking and restructuring. In Cairo, she finds inspiration in the architectural layers of Downtown, while in London, she prefers walking aimlessly to discover subtle moments. At Art Basel Qatar, her installation A House Between Two Houses presented a space shaped by emotional subjectivity and memory rather than fixed geography, engaging with concepts of transformation and decay. Watching the fair come to life in Doha and meeting fellow creators provided her with an insightful experience rooted in a rich history.

articles.originalTitle: Yohji Yamamoto Drawings - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Talk on Unpublished Yohji Yamamoto Drawings
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host an event celebrating a collection of previously unpublished drawings by designer Yohji Yamamoto.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a special talk and book celebration on Wednesday 9 December to mark the publication of Yohji Yamamoto Drawings. Author and curator Alexandre Samson will join Yohji Yamamoto's executive advisor, Caroline Fabre, at V&A South Kensington to discuss a collection of never-before-published drawings selected by Yamamoto himself. Featuring menswear and womenswear sketches designed with support from Peter Saville, the book offers insight into the designer's creative process and his exploration of fashion and form. Samson and Fabre will discuss Yamamoto's creative practice and the enduring legacy of his work during the evening event, which includes a wine reception and book signing. Priority booking for members is open, with general ticket sales beginning on 19 October, subject to availability. Ticket prices range from 15.00 to 20.00 pounds and include the post-talk reception.
